terminology.rule: Use consumption for Page 3 KPIs, labels, formulas, and charts. A source report named Yield Report keeps its source label but is not evidence for a consumption KPI until its schema is inspected.

pages.name: Risk Action Center
pages.purpose: Tell operations and procurement what needs action now: stockout, expiry, vendor risk, impacted menu items, and owner.
decisionFlow: Check stock and valid open purchase orders

visualModules.name: Global filters
visualModules.question: Which geography, outlet, category, vendor, and period are in scope?
visualModules.logic: Filter all visuals by date, region, outlet, store or kitchen, item category, super category, vendor, PO status, item code, and new or matured flag.

visualModules.name: Risk toggle
visualModules.question: Should the page show stockout, expiry, vendor, or all risks?
visualModules.logic: Use a calculated risk type to filter every KPI, table, and map view.

visualModules.name: Decision KPI row
visualModules.question: How serious is the current risk position?
visualModules.logic: Show only action KPIs for outlets, menu items, risk value, and open POs linked to risky ingredients.

visualModules.name: India outlet risk map
visualModules.question: Where are restaurant risks located?
visualModules.logic: Assign each outlet its highest current severity across stockout, expiry, and vendor risk. Requires verified outlet latitude and longitude.

visualModules.name: Risk priority stack
visualModules.question: Which risks should be handled first?
visualModules.logic: Sort by severity rank, risk value descending, then expected breach date ascending.

visualModules.name: Action center
visualModules.question: Who has to do what now?
visualModules.logic: Generate rule-based actions with owner, due date, quantity, value, PO, vendor, and impacted menu context.

visualModules.name: Stockout risk detail
visualModules.question: Which ingredients may run short and which menu items are impacted?
visualModules.logic: Compare demand plus safety with current stock plus valid open PO quantity, then calculate shortage and days cover.

visualModules.name: Menu impact detail
visualModules.question: What menu availability and forecast revenue are at risk?
visualModules.logic: Trace every short ingredient through the recipe BOM to dependent menu items and forecasted net sales.

visualModules.name: Expiry risk detail
visualModules.question: Which stock may expire or become unusable?
visualModules.logic: Use batch expiry when present. Otherwise estimate from FIFO GRN age and shelf life and label the result estimated.

visualModules.name: Vendor and PO risk overlay
visualModules.question: Is the open PO with a capable vendor?
visualModules.logic: Link risky ingredient POs to vendor OTIF, expected delivery, receipt quantity, and remaining quantity.

visualModules.name: Recommended mitigation
visualModules.question: What is the best operational response?
visualModules.logic: Start with explicit rules for stock transfer, PO expedite, new PO, alternate vendor, menu alternative, and near-expiry consumption.

rules.label: Red
rules.condition: days_cover < vendor_lead_time_days OR shortage_qty > 0 OR high_expiry_value_flag = 1 OR critical_po_vendor_otif < 0.95

rules.label: Amber
rules.condition: days_cover is between lead time and lead time plus safety days OR pending PO has amber vendor status OR expiry risk is moderate

rules.label: Green
rules.condition: available_qty covers demand plus safety AND no expiry or vendor issue exists

rules.label: Grey
rules.condition: recipe, stock, outlet mapping, active outlet, or active SKU evidence is missing

pages.name: Procurement, Vendor & Capital Control
pages.purpose: Tell procurement and finance where money is locked, which vendors are risky, which purchase orders are pending or delayed, and where prices are moving.
decisionFlow: Measure inventory value and open liability
Assess vendor delivery and fill performance

visualModules.name: Global filters
visualModules.question: Which procurement scope is being reviewed?
visualModules.logic: Filter by date, region, outlet, vendor, item category, PO status, and item code.

visualModules.name: Decision KPI row
visualModules.question: What is the financial and procurement position?
visualModules.logic: Show inventory value and open PO liability separately, plus purchase value, open POs, fill rate, OTIF, and leakage.

visualModules.name: Procurement funnel
visualModules.question: Where is the PO pipeline stuck?
visualModules.logic: Compare ordered, processed or received, pending, and delayed quantity and value.

visualModules.name: PO status distribution
visualModules.question: What is the mix of PO statuses?
visualModules.logic: Count and value purchase orders by normalized status.

visualModules.name: Pending by vendor
visualModules.question: Which vendors need follow-up?
visualModules.logic: Sum remaining quantity and open liability by vendor, with overdue state.

visualModules.name: Pending ingredient and menu impact
visualModules.question: Which pending ingredients threaten menu availability?
visualModules.logic: Link pending PO ingredients through recipe BOM and forecast demand to impacted menu count and sales risk.

visualModules.name: Expected delivery breach
visualModules.question: Which open POs are overdue?
visualModules.logic: Expected delivery date is before the as-of date and remaining quantity is greater than zero.

visualModules.name: Standing PO tracker
visualModules.question: How are standing commitments and releases progressing?
visualModules.logic: Keep separate from the normal PO funnel and show only when standing PO and release PO identifiers are available.

visualModules.name: Vendor performance matrix
visualModules.question: Which vendors are reliable and commercially efficient?
visualModules.logic: Use OTIF on one axis, normalized price variance or lead-time deviation on the other, and open liability as bubble size.

visualModules.name: Vendor scorecard
visualModules.question: What exactly is wrong with a vendor?
visualModules.logic: Show OTIF, fill rate, lead-time deviation, and return rate separately. Do not use an unsigned weighted score.

visualModules.name: Ingredient price trend
visualModules.question: Are raw material prices moving?
visualModules.logic: Compare latest normalized unit price with the previous comparable period.

visualModules.name: Vendor price comparison
visualModules.question: Are vendors charging different comparable prices for one item?
visualModules.logic: Compare normalized unit prices for the same item, UOM basis, period, and outlet scope.

visualModules.name: Top price movement
visualModules.question: Where are cost anomalies?
visualModules.logic: Rank items by normalized price change percent and purchase value impact.

visualModules.name: Inventory value by category and outlet
visualModules.question: Where is capital locked in stock?
visualModules.logic: Sum closing inventory value by item hierarchy and outlet. High value alone is neutral, not a risk.

visualModules.name: High-value and ageing stock
visualModules.question: Which high-value items need review?
visualModules.logic: Rank by inventory value and enrich with slow consumption or expiry risk where evidence exists.

rules.label: OTIF first
rules.condition: Keep OTIF, fill rate, lead time deviation, and return rate separate until score weights are signed off.

rules.label: UOM gate
rules.condition: Do not compare price until quantity and cost share a canonical UOM basis.

rules.label: Capital split
rules.condition: Display actual closing inventory value and open PO liability separately even when a combined working-capital total is shown.

pages.name: Consumption Variance & Menu Profitability
pages.purpose: Tell kitchen and supply chain what should have been consumed, actual versus theoretical variance, high-waste ingredients, and menu sales and margin.
decisionFlow: Calculate theoretical ingredient demand from sales and recipes
Relate theoretical COGS to menu profitability

visualModules.name: Global filters
visualModules.question: Which outlet, menu, ingredient, and period are in scope?
visualModules.logic: Filter by date, region, outlet, menu category, veg or non-veg, ingredient category, and store or kitchen.

visualModules.name: Decision KPI row
visualModules.question: What is the demand, consumption, and menu margin position?
visualModules.logic: Show net sales, quantity sold, theoretical COGS, consumption variance, and gross margin without repeating the full Page 4 strip.

visualModules.name: Consumption bridge
visualModules.question: How much stock should have been consumed versus actual?
visualModules.logic: Bridge opening stock, receipts, transfer in, transfer out, returns, and closing stock. Label the reduced formula when transfers are unavailable.

visualModules.name: Theoretical ingredient consumption
visualModules.question: What should have been consumed based on recipes?
visualModules.logic: Sum sold menu quantity multiplied by normalized ingredient quantity per menu unit.

visualModules.name: Consumption variance
visualModules.question: Where is actual consumption higher than theoretical?
visualModules.logic: Actual minus theoretical quantity; positive variance is valued as potential leakage using normalized average cost.

visualModules.name: Low-consumption data check
visualModules.question: Where is actual consumption lower than theoretical?
visualModules.logic: Theoretical minus actual when actual is lower. Treat as an amber process or data check, not a favorable result.

visualModules.name: High-waste ingredients
visualModules.question: Which ingredients repeatedly leak?
visualModules.logic: Rank by leakage value, leakage percent, and recurrence across outlets.

visualModules.name: Theoretical COGS by menu item
visualModules.question: What should each menu item cost?
visualModules.logic: Sum normalized recipe ingredient quantity multiplied by normalized average inventory cost.

visualModules.name: Gross margin by menu item
visualModules.question: Which menu items are commercially strong or weak?
visualModules.logic: Net sales minus theoretical COGS, with margin percent calculated against net sales.

visualModules.name: Menu BCG matrix
visualModules.question: Which menu items should be pushed, reviewed, or rationalized?
visualModules.logic: Use quantity or net sales on the demand axis, gross margin percent on the profitability axis, and net sales as size.

visualModules.name: Sales trend
visualModules.question: How is demand moving?
visualModules.logic: Trend net sales and quantity by date.

visualModules.name: Sales by category
visualModules.question: Which menu categories drive contribution?
visualModules.logic: Category net sales divided by total net sales in the selected scope.

visualModules.name: Item ranking
visualModules.question: What sells most and least?
visualModules.logic: Use one visual with a metric toggle for quantity, net sales, margin, and COGS.

visualModules.name: Veg and non-veg sales mix
visualModules.question: What is the menu mix?
visualModules.logic: Compare each menu classification's net sales with total net sales.

visualModules.name: Outlet item heatmap
visualModules.question: Where are localized demand differences?
visualModules.logic: Matrix outlet by menu item or category using quantity or net sales.

rules.label: Month-to-date
rules.condition: Do not call actual variance final unless an actual stock count is available.

rules.label: Month-end
rules.condition: Use month-end closing stock as the primary reconciliation checkpoint.

rules.label: Attribution limit
rules.condition: Stock alone cannot allocate physical ingredient consumption exactly among multiple menu items.

rules.label: UOM gate
rules.condition: Do not publish variance or COGS when recipe and inventory units cannot be reconciled.

pages.name: SCM Descriptive Explorer & Data Quality
pages.purpose: Provide a clean drilldown and export layer with descriptive KPIs, trends, item, vendor and outlet detail, and data-quality exceptions.

visualModules.name: Global filters
visualModules.question: What detailed slice should be inspected?
visualModules.logic: Filter by date, outlet, region, store, category, vendor, PO status, and item.

visualModules.name: Executive KPI strip
visualModules.question: What is the basic SCM position?
visualModules.logic: Show the full descriptive strip only on Page 4: sales, quantity, menu items, inventory, PO, pending, GRN, vendor, negative stock, and zero stock totals.

visualModules.name: Trend cards
visualModules.question: How are core measures changing?
visualModules.logic: Trend sales, inventory value, PO value, pending PO, and GRN value over comparable periods.

visualModules.name: Sales detail
visualModules.question: What was sold by outlet, menu, and category?
visualModules.logic: Exportable aggregation with net sales, quantity, average selling price, and category contribution.

visualModules.name: Inventory detail
visualModules.question: What stock is currently available?
visualModules.logic: Show quantity, value, and average price by outlet, item, and category.

visualModules.name: PO detail
visualModules.question: What was ordered and what is pending?
visualModules.logic: Line-level ordered, processed, remaining, pending value, status, and ageing.

visualModules.name: GRN and entry detail
visualModules.question: What was received or returned?
visualModules.logic: Show receipt quantity and value, returns, unit price, vendor, and PO linkage where available.

visualModules.name: Vendor detail
visualModules.question: Which vendors are active and how much business do they have?
visualModules.logic: Show active state, PO count, PO value, pending value, and fill rate.

visualModules.name: Negative stock exception
visualModules.question: Where is stock data broken or a process failing?
visualModules.logic: Count and expose inventory rows with normalized closing quantity below zero.

visualModules.name: Zero stock with demand exception
visualModules.question: Which zero-stock items may hurt sales?
visualModules.logic: Find zero stock with positive forecast demand or positive historical demand evidence.

visualModules.name: Missing recipe exception
visualModules.question: Which sold menu items cannot be converted to ingredient demand?
visualModules.logic: Find sold menu item identifiers without a valid recipe BOM mapping.

visualModules.name: Missing item or category mapping exception
visualModules.question: Which operational items lack master data?
visualModules.logic: Find purchase, receipt, movement, or inventory item identifiers absent from the item master.

visualModules.name: UOM mismatch exception
visualModules.question: Which items can distort consumption or price comparison?
visualModules.logic: Find the same item in multiple units without an approved conversion factor.

visualModules.name: PO missing expected delivery exception
visualModules.question: Which open POs cannot be risk-scored?
visualModules.logic: Find open PO lines with no expected delivery date.

visualModules.name: Export and drilldown
visualModules.question: Can users inspect and download clean details?
visualModules.logic: Provide governed exports for sales, inventory, PO, GRN, risk, and data-quality detail.

rules.label: Descriptive only
rules.condition: Keep descriptive totals separate from Page 1 action prioritization.

rules.label: Exception traceability
rules.condition: Every data-quality tile must drill to the exact rows and missing keys behind it.

kpis.name: Outlets at Risk
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct active outlets with at least one current purple, red, or amber supply-chain risk.
caveats: Requires a verified active outlet master and one deterministic highest-severity rule per outlet.

kpis.name: Menu Items at Risk
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct menu items dependent on an ingredient carrying an active supply or expiry risk.
caveats: Requires stable menu-to-recipe and recipe-to-ingredient identifiers.

kpis.name: Stockout Risk Value
kpis.businessDefinition: Forecasted net sales of menu items dependent on ingredients with a positive projected shortage.
caveats: This is revenue exposure, not guaranteed lost sales.
Forecast horizon and double-count handling need sign-off.

kpis.name: Expiry Risk Value
kpis.businessDefinition: Value of stock expected to expire within the approved threshold.
kpis.grain: Outlet, store, item, batch or estimate date
caveats: Exact only with batch or expiry data; otherwise label FIFO and shelf-life output estimated.

kpis.name: Open Risk-Linked PO Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct open purchase orders linked to ingredients carrying an active risk.
caveats: Needs reliable PO status and ingredient identifiers.

kpis.name: Forecast Menu Quantity
kpis.businessDefinition: Predicted menu-item demand over the selected risk horizon.
caveats: Forecast model, horizon, and confidence interval are not yet approved.

kpis.name: Projected Shortage Quantity
kpis.businessDefinition: Ingredient requirement including safety stock that is not covered by current stock and valid open PO quantity.
kpis.grain: Outlet, store, ingredient, forecast horizon, canonical UOM
caveats: Valid PO must arrive before the expected consumption date.
All quantities require canonical UOM conversion.

kpis.name: Days Cover
kpis.businessDefinition: Days that available inventory and usable inbound quantity can cover normalized daily consumption.
caveats: Define the daily-consumption lookback or forecast basis before publication.

kpis.name: Monthly Purchase Value
kpis.businessDefinition: Value of purchase activity in the selected month using the approved PO or receipt basis.
caveats: Business must choose ordered, received, or invoiced value as the primary basis.

kpis.name: Closing Inventory Value
kpis.businessDefinition: Value of normalized closing stock at the selected checkpoint.
caveats: Prefer the source closing amount when its costing basis reconciles.

kpis.name: Open PO Liability
kpis.businessDefinition: Remaining committed purchase value on open or partially received PO lines.
caveats: Exclude cancelled, closed, and expired commitments based on normalized status.

kpis.name: Working Capital Locked
kpis.businessDefinition: Combined view of closing inventory value and open PO liability, with both components still displayed separately.
caveats: Do not hide the two components inside only one total.

kpis.name: Open PO Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct purchase orders with at least one open or partially received line.
caveats: Status normalization requires UAT evidence.

kpis.name: PO Fill Rate
kpis.businessDefinition: Share of ordered quantity that was processed or received on comparable closed and partial PO lines.
caveats: Confirm whether processed quantity equals accepted receipt quantity.

kpis.name: Vendor OTIF
kpis.businessDefinition: Share of eligible closed PO lines received on or before expected delivery and in full.
kpis.formula: COUNT(po_line WHERE on_time = 1 AND in_full = 1) / NULLIF(COUNT(eligible_closed_po_line), 0)
caveats: Cannot be published from approximate vendor-item-date matching.
Needs PO-line-to-GRN linkage and an approved in-full tolerance.

kpis.name: Lead Time Deviation
kpis.businessDefinition: Difference between actual accepted delivery date and expected delivery date.
kpis.grain: PO line or accepted receipt line
caveats: Define treatment of partial receipts and early delivery.

kpis.name: Vendor Return Rate
kpis.businessDefinition: Returned quantity as a share of received plus returned quantity for a vendor.
caveats: Return reason and original receipt linkage are desirable for diagnosis.

kpis.name: Purchase Price Change %
kpis.businessDefinition: Change in comparable normalized unit price from the prior approved period.
kpis.grain: Item, canonical UOM, vendor or market scope, period
caveats: Never compare different pack or UOM bases without conversion.

kpis.name: Financial Leakage
kpis.businessDefinition: Observed return, return tax, expiry, and wastage value within the available source scope.
kpis.grain: Outlet, item, vendor where applicable, period
caveats: Display source coverage so missing expiry or wastage does not appear as zero loss.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.businessDefinition: Net sales for valid sold menu-item lines in the selected scope.
caveats: Void, return, discount, and tax treatment must reconcile to Restroworks totals.

kpis.name: Quantity Sold
kpis.businessDefinition: Valid sold menu-item quantity in the selected scope.
caveats: Combo, modifier, void, and return handling require schema validation.

kpis.name: Theoretical Consumption Quantity
kpis.businessDefinition: Ingredient quantity expected to be consumed from menu-item sales and the effective recipe BOM.
caveats: Recipe effective dating, base quantity, wastage factor, combos, and modifiers need validation.

kpis.name: Theoretical COGS
kpis.businessDefinition: Expected ingredient cost of sold menu items using normalized recipe quantity and approved average ingredient cost.
kpis.grain: Date, outlet, menu item and ingredient
caveats: Average cost basis and recipe effective date require sign-off.

kpis.name: Actual Consumption Quantity
kpis.businessDefinition: Inventory quantity consumed after accounting for opening, receipts, transfers, returns, and closing stock.
kpis.formula: opening_qty + grn_qty + transfer_in_qty - transfer_out_qty - return_qty - closing_qty
kpis.grain: Outlet, store, ingredient, stock-count period, canonical UOM
caveats: If transfer data is unavailable, use previous closing plus entry minus current closing and label reduced completeness.
Month-to-date output is provisional without a physical stock count.

kpis.name: Consumption Variance Quantity
kpis.businessDefinition: Difference between actual and theoretical ingredient consumption.
kpis.grain: Outlet, store, ingredient, stock-count period, canonical UOM
caveats: Positive means higher actual usage; negative is a data or process check, not automatically favorable.

kpis.name: Consumption Leakage Value
kpis.businessDefinition: Value of positive actual-over-theoretical consumption variance.
caveats: Use consumption terminology consistently in every chart and export.

kpis.name: Low Consumption Check
kpis.businessDefinition: Quantity by which actual consumption is below theoretical consumption.
caveats: Treat as an amber data, stock-count, recipe, or process exception.

kpis.name: Menu Gross Margin
kpis.businessDefinition: Net sales less theoretical recipe COGS for a menu item.
caveats: This is recipe gross margin, not full contribution margin.

kpis.name: Menu Gross Margin %
kpis.businessDefinition: Theoretical menu gross margin as a share of net sales.
caveats: Exclude or separately handle zero and negative net sales.

kpis.name: Negative Stock Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Count of item-location checkpoints with normalized closing quantity below zero.
caveats: Show on Page 1 only when the exception creates actual menu risk.

kpis.name: Zero Stock with Demand Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Count of item locations with zero stock and positive forecast or approved historical demand evidence.
caveats: Demand basis must be visible in drilldown.

kpis.name: Sold Items Missing Recipe Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct sold menu items without a valid recipe BOM mapping.
kpis.formula: COUNT_DISTINCT(menu_item_id WHERE sold_qty > 0 AND recipe_id IS NULL)
caveats: Use stable identifiers; name-only misses may be false exceptions.

kpis.name: Operational Items Missing Master Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct purchase, receipt, movement, or inventory item identifiers absent from the canonical item master.
caveats: Report source system and source field for every exception.

kpis.name: UOM Mismatch Count
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct items observed in multiple units without a complete approved conversion path.
caveats: Pack size and density conversions may require item-specific rules.

kpis.name: Open POs Missing Expected Delivery
kpis.businessDefinition: Distinct open purchase orders that cannot be delivery-risk scored because expected delivery is absent.
kpis.formula: COUNT_DISTINCT(po_number WHERE po_is_open = 1 AND expected_delivery_date IS NULL)
caveats: A PO with every line closed is not an exception even if the header date is blank.

Do not spend current discovery time on settlement, tax, loyalty, booking, or compliance reports unless a selected control-tower KPI needs them.

modelRevision.rationale: The current layered structure is reusable, but its synthetic outlet mappings and approximate joins are not production-safe. Revising the core avoids both duplicate models and carrying known assumptions forward.
retain: Layered RAW to STD to DIM/FACT to SUM convention
Core sales, purchase-order, receipt, closing-inventory, recipe, item, vendor, and date concepts
Existing query naming and dependency ordering where semantics remain valid
revise: Replace three hardcoded outlet unions and CASE mappings with source-driven outlet identity and outlet master joins
Replace name-based menu and ingredient joins with canonical identifiers plus an explicit unresolved-mapping queue
Remove the arbitrary quantity <= 10 low-stock rule and calculate demand-aware shortage and days cover
Block OTIF and delivery metrics until PO line and GRN linkage is proven; retire approximate vendor-item-date matching from KPI use
Add explicit valid-open-PO timing so inbound quantity is counted only when it arrives before demand
Separate descriptive inventory pressure from predicted stockout risk
defer: Weighted vendor criticality score until business weights are approved
Exact expiry risk without batch or expiry evidence
Standing PO analytics without release identifiers
Menu-level allocation of physical ingredient variance

deliveryPlan.pocIngestion: Export a minimal validated CSV set from Restroworks, import into stable Zoho tables, and use replace or update modes with explicit keys. Keep a repeatable import manifest and reconciliation totals.
deliveryPlan.productionIngestion: Prefer Restroworks APIs for validated item-level sales and inventory modes, then schedule missing report exports through a persistent feed, cloud storage, SFTP, Databridge, or a small controlled middleware. Manual local uploads are not an automation design.
deliveryPlan.analytics: Use Zoho Analytics for governed tables, query tables, calculations, standard charts, drilldowns, exports, data refresh monitoring, and row-level access.
deliveryPlan.presentation: Prototype the four pages in Zoho first. Use embedded or white-label Zoho views inside a custom shell only if the action queue, cross-page RAG interactions, map behavior, or presentation fidelity cannot be achieved cleanly in the native portal.
